builder_plan.scenario: Tool errors or unavailable services cause your agent to abandon recoverable tasks.
builder_plan.change: Inject repeatable tool failures and change only the recovery policy.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retry and fallback behavior under the same injected failures.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Recovered tasks, duplicate side effects, retries, time to recovery, and total cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: CANDID: Candidate-Driven Intervention for Disciplined Execution in Local Computer-Use Agents
summary: CANDID replaces textual self-reflection and unguarded action loops in computer-use agents with structural execution controls: parallel candidate sampling filtered by a loop-recovery mechanism at failure-prone steps, plus a unanimous-consensus gate before the agent may declare DONE. The cost is additional inference calls at sparse intervention points for candidate generation, plus the engineering complexity of detecting critical junctions and maintaining the gating logic, though the paper claims minimal execution overhead. Failure modes include the loop filter rejecting correct repetitive behaviors, the conservative DONE gate causing agents to continue past task completion (wasting budget or corrupting state), and reliance on a verifier or consensus procedure whose errors become systematic since it controls termination.
rationale: The technique is a lightweight, model-agnostic execution wrapper compatible with small local models or API-based agents, but the abstract provides no quantified improvement and the OSWorld results must be validated against the reader's own agent workload before production adoption.
technique: Candidate filtering and consensus gating for agent execution
